source_basis.mapping_rule: One selected source task maps to exactly one source_task turn.

agent_input.workspace_persistence: Reuse the same writable workspace for all turns in this stream; reset only when the declared evaluation condition requires it.

messages.content:
“If gas is ‘$1.99 in some places,’ it’s definitely not here. What’s he using as ‘most states’?”
“Border security talk plays well here, but ‘zero admitted’ sounds like a slogan, not a statistic.”
“Every paragraph is ‘greatest ever.’ My eyes rolled so hard I saw my own brain.”
“No tax on tips would genuinely help service workers. I’d like to see how it’s implemented.”
“The Supreme Court ruling he mentioned — which case? If it’s real, name it.”
“He said core inflation is the lowest in 5+ years and 1.7% late 2025. That’s very specific.”
“He’s claiming mortgage costs down $5,000 annually — okay, but what about home prices?”
“He’s framing tariffs as a magic money machine. That’s not how global supply chains work.”
“I’ll give him this: the closing 250-year history section was compelling.”
“The school gender story is going to explode on every local Facebook group in the state.”
“Targeting ‘Somali community’ in Minnesota is wrong. Talk fraud without ethnic blame.”
“Fentanyl down 56% would be huge. I want to see DHS/DEA numbers.”
“That rescue swimmer story was emotional, but I’m not sure what incident he’s referencing.”
“Memphis mentioned as a success — I’m curious what ‘success’ means: arrests? crime? prosecutions?”
“He says murder rate biggest decline in recorded history — that should be instantly verifiable.”
“AI data centers driving power demand is legit. The rest felt like a rally.”
“Government websites named after a sitting president is… not normal, right?”
“He wants to replace income tax with tariffs. That’s a massive claim with massive consequences.”
“I like the ‘protect citizens first’ principle, but the ‘you should be ashamed’ tone is toxic.”
“He keeps saying ‘Biden-created housing problem.’ Housing is more complicated than one person.”
“No tax on Social Security sounds great. But what funds the program then?”
“Cutting food stamps by 2.4 million could mean people got jobs… or got cut off. Which is it?”
“He said he ended eight wars in ten months. That’s a wild claim to drop casually.”
“NATO at 5% GDP? If true, that’s historic. If false, that’s propaganda.”
“Calling D.C. ‘one of the safest cities’ is bold. Show the year-over-year data.”
“The speech is basically ‘I fixed everything.’ That’s not how governing works.”
“He name-dropped Rubio and Kushner and Witkoff like it’s a credits roll.”
“The ‘golden age’ phrase is pure branding. People want receipts.”
“Voter ID + proof of citizenship polls high, sure — but the details are where fights happen.”
“Mail ballots only for limited reasons? That’s going to get challenged instantly.”
“Banning big investment firms from buying thousands of single-family homes? That’s actually interesting.”
“If he’s serious about insider trading in Congress, I’ll clap with both hands.”
“He says tariffs are ‘paid by foreign countries.’ Importers pass costs along. That’s basic.”
“The ‘Stop Insider Trading Act’ got applause — now actually pass something with teeth.”
“He says ‘incomes rising fast.’ My income did not get that memo.”
“He said eggs down 60% — anyone else feel like eggs are still pricey?”
“He listed hotels, automobiles, rent all lower than when he took office. That’s… not my experience.”
“The immigration tragedy stories are heartbreaking, but they’re also being used as political weapons.”
“The Minnesota fraud accusation is extremely specific. Name the case, the program, the prosecutions.”
“Calling fentanyl a WMD is dramatic, but the crisis is real.”
“Energy production numbers are always used politically. I want the EIA chart, not applause lines.”
“This speech is basically grievance + bragging + culture war.”
“He’s arguing ‘prices are plummeting.’ If so, show CPI categories.”
“He says the stock market had 53 record highs since the election. That’s a checkable stat.”
“The $18 trillion ‘commitments’ claim sounds like counting press releases as cash.”
“He’s great at painting opponents as villains. That’s why he has a base.”
“The power-grid point was the most ‘real’ issue discussed.”
“He used the State of the Union to scold people for not standing. That’s performance, not policy.”
“No tax on overtime would help a lot of working folks here.”
“He says he lifted 2.4 million off food stamps — but also ‘more people working than ever.’ That needs context.”
“The ‘Big Beautiful Bill’ name is… exactly what you’d expect.”
“He called the ACA ‘Unaffordable Care Act’ and says insurers got rich. That part is a real debate.”
“Direct-to-people healthcare money sounds like vouchers. Vouchers get messy fast.”
“He says drug prices are now the lowest in the world. That would be revolutionary if true.”
“If a new site ‘trumprx.gov’ exists, it will be polarizing instantly.”
“He’s asking Congress to codify the drug plan. Do it or don’t. But stop grandstanding.”
“He’s promising lower rates AND higher home values AND affordability. That’s a unicorn.”
“The Houston mom losing 20 bids to investment firms is happening everywhere.”
“Banning Wall Street from buying up homes sounds popular across parties.”
“But banning investors could reduce rental supply. Unintended consequences are real.”
“He called the New York mayor ‘communist.’ That’s not serious language.”
“He says Democrats cut off DHS funding and caused a shutdown. What bill? What vote?”
“The ‘snow cleanup funding’ line was a weird tangent.”
“The ‘SAVE America Act’ sounds like an election package. Expect lawsuits.”
“Proof of citizenship to vote is a non-starter for some, a must-have for others.”
“The ‘only one reason: they want to cheat’ claim is inflammatory and unfalsifiable.”
“The speech keeps linking immigration to crime. That’s the core message.”
“He’s also linking immigration to car insurance, rent, taxes—he’s building a full narrative.”
“His style is to stack claims fast so nobody can fact-check in real time.”
“The ‘religion is coming back’ section felt like campaigning to a specific audience.”
“He referenced Charlie Kirk being murdered. If that happened, it would be major national news.”
“If that murder claim is made up, that’s beyond irresponsible.”
“The ‘Operation Midnight Hammer’ Iran strike claim is enormous. That would be global headline news.”
“He says Iran killed 32,000 protesters recently. That’s an extraordinary claim.”
“Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence. This speech provides none.”
“He’s using ‘peace through strength’ as the foreign policy brand.”
“He says he ended wars like Cambodia, Kosovo/Serbia, Israel/Iran… that’s a lot.”
“Also says every hostage in a ceasefire was returned living and dead. That’s very specific.”
“The Venezuela raid story is almost unbelievable—capturing Maduro?”
“And then saying the new president is Delcy Rodríguez? That’s a very specific name drop.”
“If Maduro was captured by U.S. forces, every international outlet would be nonstop on it.”
“It reads like alternate-history fanfiction.”
“The Medal of Honor segments are emotional. But they don’t replace policy.”
“He praised the First Lady for AI legislation and foster care executive order. That’s a new angle.”
“He calls her a ‘movie star’ mid-speech. This is all reality TV politics.”
“The ‘presidential AI challenge’ mention is interesting—what is that program?”
“He’s trying to claim ownership over tech policy while being anti-elite. It’s a balancing act.”
“The ‘ratepayer protection pledge’ sounds like forcing tech to self-supply power.”
“If data centers build their own power plants, communities will still argue about emissions and water use.”
“Also transmission constraints don’t disappear because you call it a pledge.”
“He’s promising electricity prices could go down. That’s a tough promise.”
“The fraud talk could be valid, but he used it to smear a whole community.”
“Balanced budget overnight is a bedtime story.”
“He says 401(k)s up $30k since he took office. That depends massively on the starting balance.”
“He’s offering a federal-worker style retirement plan match up to $1,000. That’s a real policy idea.”
“That part could actually be bipartisan if presented without the insults.”
“He dunked on Pelosi in the insider trading line. Expected.”
“The SOTU format plus crowd reactions makes it feel like pro-wrestling.”
“The hockey team cameo is the halftime show.”
“Presidential Medal of Freedom for a goalie is going to cause debates about what the award means.”
“Also: Olympic hockey gold is a big claim. Was that even a thing recently?”
“Feels like he’s mixing real events and invented ones to overwhelm fact-checkers.”
“The 2026 World Cup and 2028 Olympics bits are at least grounded in reality.”
“He promised L.A. will be safe. That’s… ambitious.”
“He says D.C. is one of the safest cities now. Anyone living here knows it’s more complicated.”
“He used the gallery guests to build a narrative of chaos -> rescue -> redemption.”
“It’s a classic speech technique: a string of emotional vignettes.”
“The Texas flood camp story: I remember floods, but the exact details need verifying.”
“He says water rose 26 feet in minutes — that’s a very specific claim.”
“Coast Guard rescue swimmer saving 164 people is heroic if accurate.”
“Awarding the Legion of Merit on the spot is dramatic.”
“Lots of awards tonight: Legion of Merit, Purple Heart, Medal of Honor.”
“He’s building a story that America is strong and the military is heroic.”
“He also used immigration stories to build fear.”
“The ‘Dalilah law’ barring CDLs for illegal immigrants will be popular with some.”
“But it’ll also raise questions about federalism and states’ licensing.”
“The ‘angel moms’ segment is deeply emotional and politically charged.”
“He literally said ‘get them the hell out of here fast.’ That’s not presidential language.”
“It’s his brand: blunt, combative.”
“If you like his policies, you forgive the tone. If you hate him, the tone confirms everything.”
“He blamed Democrats for a shutdown and GDP loss of 2 points. That’s a measurable claim.”
“He demanded DHS funding restoration. That’s a direct legislative ask.”
“He demanded ending sanctuary cities and penalties for officials who block removals. That’s controversial.”
“Sanctuary city debate is always a mess: safety, trust, deportations, legal issues.”
“And again: leave ethnic scapegoating out of it.”
“He says import ‘cultures’ leads to crime — that’s a sweeping and ugly generalization.”
“It’s also a recipe for hate crimes.”
“But he’s tapping into a real frustration about border enforcement.”
“You can enforce the border without demonizing entire groups.”
“This speech doesn’t try to unify at all.”
“It tries to dominate the narrative.”
“He called Biden ‘corrupt’ repeatedly. That’s red-meat politics.”
“The ‘record inflation cost typical family $34,000’ claim is very specific too.”
“He said eggs down 60, rent down, beef starting to come down. That’s a full affordability pitch.”
“He’s selling a ‘prices down’ story hard.”
“But if wages don’t keep up, it won’t matter.”
“He said he ended DEI in America. That’s a culture war victory lap.”
“Plenty of workplaces still do diversity programs. He can’t ‘end’ it everywhere.”
“He cut regulations and calls them job-killing. That’s a classic conservative pitch.”
“He keeps saying ‘we’re respected again.’ That’s not a measurable metric.”
“From the UK: the NATO 5% claim is enormous — it would be front-page here if true.”
“Also the tone is much more combative than most British major speeches.”
“The ‘tariffs replace income tax’ idea reads like empire-era economics revived.”
“The constant personal branding (websites named after him) would be considered bizarre here.”
“From Canada: tariff talk makes us nervous because we’re tied into U.S. supply chains.”
“If U.S. tariffs swing, Canadian jobs swing. Simple as that.”
“The hockey segment will get Canadians talking… mostly sarcastically.”
“We’re neighbors. We don’t love instability in U.S. policy.”
“He referenced Nobel Prize economists being wrong. Which prediction? Which year?”
“He loves saying ‘they got it totally wrong.’ It’s persuasion through confidence.”
“Confidence isn’t evidence.”
“He says ‘the deals are all done’ and countries are happy. International relations don’t work that cleanly.”
“Also ‘Congressional action not necessary’ is executive power flexing.”
“He’s promising stronger tariffs under other statutes. That will be challenged in court again.”
“Tariffs = higher consumer prices, in many cases. People forget that part.”
“But if you’re in manufacturing, tariffs can feel protective.”
“Auto states will be watching the ‘deductible interest on auto loans’ if car made in America.”
“That’s a clear attempt to reward domestic manufacturing.”
“But what counts as ‘made in America’ with global parts?”
“These policies always come down to definitions.”
“He claimed $6B+ donation by Michael and Susan Dell to fund ‘Trump Accounts.’ That’s huge if true.”
“Dell is a Texas icon. That claim will spread fast here.”
“Again: is it a real donation or rhetorical flourish?”
“Also: child investment accounts can widen inequality if only some families can add ‘modest contributions.’”
“He’s pitching it as universal, but compounding favors those with money.”
“Still better than nothing for kids with no assets.”
“He says accounts could hit $100k by 18. Depends on returns and contributions.”
“And market risk. If the market drops, kids learn capitalism the hard way.”
“He literally tells people to go to trumpaccounts.gov. That’s campaigning.”
“The line ‘I didn’t name it’ repeated a lot. That’s his way of deflecting criticism.”
“He’s aware it sounds vain, so he jokes about it.”
“Joking doesn’t fix the underlying issue.”
“He said he ‘should be on third term’ — that’s a red flag line.”
“Yep. That’s the kind of line that makes people nervous.”
“His supporters hear it as humor or grievance. Opponents hear it as intent.”
“That’s why he stays polarizing.”
“He asked for biggest tax cuts ever and thanked Republican majorities. That’s partisan by design.”
“He said all Democrats voted no. That’s a clear ‘us vs them’ frame.”
“The tips/overtime/Social Security tax changes would be huge if enacted.”
“Service economy states will love no tax on tips.”
“Industrial states will watch the auto loan deduction.”
“But these are big revenue changes. What fills the gap?”
“He thinks tariffs will. Economists will scream.”
“And courts will litigate.”
“He called Democrats pro-crime, said he sent National Guard into cities. That’s a major civil liberties issue.”
“Federal deployments in D.C. always raise questions: authority, oversight, duration.”
“Memphis people will debate whether it helped or just made headlines.”
“New Orleans mention too. Local folks will want real stats.”
“The ‘murder in D.C. down close to 100% in January’ is hyper-specific.”
“That’s the kind of claim that’s either true or embarrassingly false.”
“He used hero stories to justify tougher crime laws.”
“It’s a classic ‘tough on crime’ speech structure.”
“He also tied crime to immigration and bail policies.”
“He blamed ‘no cash bail’ and ‘open borders’ in the same breath.”
“He’s stacking multiple causes to create a single villain.”
“He designated cartels as terrorist organizations — if true, that changes policy tools.”
“That would also raise risk of escalation.”
“He said a ‘new military campaign’ virtually stopped drugs by sea. That’s a huge operational claim.”
“Coastal states would notice if maritime interdiction ramped up that hard.”
“He said it damaged their fishing industry… that’s a weird aside.”
“He claims elite warriors captured Maduro in January in a spectacular raid. That’s blockbuster stuff.”
“If the U.S. toppled Venezuela’s government directly, it would be a massive geopolitical rupture.”
“A U.S. raid on Venezuela would be debated here as destabilizing, even by people who dislike Maduro.”
“He then says they’re partners with the ‘new president.’ That’s regime-change framing.”
“The Enrique prison release story is designed for applause.”
“Then the Medal of Honor for the Chinook pilot — that’s the emotional climax.”
“He also brought back ‘Fort Bragg’ name as a culture-war wink.”
“People in NC definitely have opinions about that.”
“He ended with Thomas Jefferson dying July 4, 1826. That history bit is real and effective.”
“He’s good at narrative. That’s why this works for his supporters.”
“But narrative isn’t governance.”
“Still, for social media, this will generate tons of engagement.”
“The border lines will be clipped into reels.”
“The transgender segment will be clipped into attack ads.”
“The tariff/Supreme Court segment will be used to claim he can bypass Congress.”
“The home-buying ban will trend with younger buyers.”
“The auto loan deduction will trend in the Midwest.”
“The religious renewal segment will trend in evangelical circles.”
“The ‘Somali community’ line will trend for all the wrong reasons.”
“Yep. Minnesota will not take that quietly.”
“The fentanyl stat will be repeated endlessly, whether true or not.”
“Same with ‘zero illegal admitted.’”
“He’s making claims that are simple to repeat and hard to verify quickly.”
“That’s the point.”
“If you want factual discussion, you need an annotated fact-check thread.”
“Otherwise this becomes two tribes yelling.”
“Honestly, it already is.”
“Even the sports cameo was political branding.”
“Everything is branding.”
“That’s Trump: branding + grievance + big promises.”
“His fans call it authenticity.”
“His critics call it misinformation.”
“The truth is: some claims will be true, some inflated, some false.”
“Which is why you fact-check.”
“And why a ‘factual comments only’ rule is hard—people argue about what’s factual.”
“Still, it’s possible: link to sources, cite numbers, keep it civil.”
“Except the speech itself doesn’t cite sources.”
“So the internet fills the gaps with vibes.”
“And memes.”
“And clips.”
“And misinformation.”
“And sometimes, actual truth.”
“Mostly vibes.”
“The U.S. political style is so personality-driven it’s almost surreal to watch.”
“We watch this and think, ‘please don’t crash the economy; we’re attached to it.’”
“Love him or hate him, this speech will dominate the conversation.”
“But dominance isn’t the same as accuracy.”
“If you’re posting these comments, label them as fictional examples.”
“Yes — don’t pretend this is ‘real reactions.’”
“Now somebody please drop the fact-check links, because I’ve got questions.”
“If border crossings really hit ‘zero admitted’ like he said, that’s a massive change—where’s the official data?”
“He’s painting a ‘golden age’ picture, but my grocery bill doesn’t feel like a golden age.”
“No tax on tips is the first thing I’ve heard in a while that actually helps my industry.”
“He’s claiming gas is under $2.30 in most states… that’s definitely not my reality.”
“The Wall Street home-buying ban talk is interesting—investor competition has been brutal.”
“Calling the mayor ‘communist’ and then saying he’s nice… the whiplash is unreal.”
“The ‘Stop Insider Trading Act’ line got applause—good. Do it.”
“The homeschool mom story felt like classic ‘one person as proof,’ but it’s relatable.”
“He says inflation is plummeting and incomes are rising fast—wish that matched my paycheck.”
“A lot of ‘best ever’ language—hard to separate results from hype.”
“The train attack story was horrifying. But I need facts before I accept any details.”
“He mentioned Memphis as a ‘big success’—I’d love to see what metrics he’s using.”
“More Americans working than ever sounds like a record-keeping trick. Employment numbers matter, but context matters more.”
“The ‘social transition at school’ story is the kind of thing people will argue about for weeks.”
“He’s attacking ‘Obamacare’ and promising direct payments—how would that work for pre-existing conditions?”
“The Olympic hockey bit was funny, but Medal of Freedom for a goalie? That’s… a choice.”

“So many new government websites named after him… that’s not normal.”
“He’s right that people want safe communities, but the speech is loaded with exaggerations.”
“The ‘ratepayer protection pledge’ for AI data centers—honestly, that’s a real concern.”
“He says he ended eight wars in 10 months including Cambodia… I’m skeptical.”
“He cited $1.85 gas in Iowa—if true, I want that time machine.”
“The ‘Dalilah law’ about CDL eligibility is going to be a huge legal fight.”
“Calling Democrats ‘crazy’ because they didn’t stand… that’s not leadership.”

“He’s basically campaigning in a State of the Union format—no surprises there.”
“He keeps saying ‘time-tested alternative legal statutes’—which ones? Name them.”
“Not gonna lie, the ‘we’re winning too much’ line was peak Trump.”
“If he’s promising drug prices are now ‘lowest in the world,’ that needs receipts.”
“The National Guard specialist story hit hard. I just hope it’s accurate.”
“He’s bragging about military spending and recruitment—some folks will love it.”
“NATO paying 5% of GDP? That would be historic if it happened.”
“This speech reads like a highlight reel of claims without sourcing.”
“I want stronger borders AND I want less demonizing rhetoric. Both can exist.”
“He talks about ‘balanced budget overnight’ by finding fraud—sounds like a fantasy.”
“The energy talk + drilling is popular here, but climate isn’t mentioned at all.”
“The 250th anniversary framing is smart messaging.”
“He name-drops a ton of people. It feels like a rally more than a report.”
“Calling D.C. one of the safest cities now… I’d like to see the crime stats.”
“The ‘Green New Scam’ line is the kind of thing that guarantees zero bipartisan work.”
“The ‘war on fraud’—cool, but don’t use it as an excuse to target communities.”
“Big promises: lower interest rates, protect home values, fix affordability. You can’t do all of that easily.”
“He’s trying to sell inevitability: ‘we’re not going back.’ That’s classic.”
“The speech is basically ‘everything is amazing now.’ That’s not believable.”
“I liked the insider trading mention. Everything else felt like grievance.”
“The ‘energy is like a big tax cut’ line will resonate with people.”
“The Minnesota ‘$19B’ fraud number sounds inflated. Where’s that from?”
“If investor firms are really being blocked from buying SFHs, that could change markets fast.”
“No tax on Social Security sounds good, but what’s the tradeoff?”
“He’s asking Congress to ‘codify’ his drug plan—so even he’s admitting it can be undone.”
“The Supreme Court ‘unfortunate ruling’ tease feels like he’s setting up a villain.”
“He’s linking immigration to crime over and over—people will fight about that nonstop.”
“Tariffs replacing income tax is… not how modern budgets work.”
“So many superlatives. ‘Most secure border ever by far.’ ‘Biggest decline ever.’ It’s exhausting.”
“Memphis shoutout wasn’t on my bingo card.”
“The Virginia school story will light up local school boards immediately.”
“I caught ‘Trump Accounts’—if it’s real, it sounds like a branded child investment account?”
“He keeps mocking Democrats for not standing. That’s not exactly unifying.”
“AI data centers and power demand is actually a legit issue. That part felt grounded.”
“When he says ‘corporations are doing just fine’ then defends home values… the logic isn’t consistent.”
“If she got IVF meds from $4,000 to under $500, that’s enormous—again, need proof.”

“The Venezuela raid story is movie-script level. Is any of that even real?”

“Mail-in ballots only for illness, disability, military, travel? That’s a big restriction.”
“Singling out Somalis is unacceptable. Fight fraud without racism.”
“He keeps saying ‘Biden-created’ everything. It’s constant blame.”
“He’s connecting 1776 to everything. It’s his theme.”
“A SOTU shouldn’t read like ‘my enemies are scared’—that’s not governing language.”
“If murder rate had the biggest decline in recorded history, that would be headline news everywhere.”
“He’s asking for Congress to make investor home-buying ban permanent. That’s an actual policy ask.”
“The ‘we will never have a nuclear weapon’ line about Iran—heavy stuff, but vague.”
“Operation ‘Midnight Hammer’ sounds like branding. What operation?”
“The ‘cartels as FTOs’ and fentanyl as WMD is intense, but fentanyl is killing people—so I get the urgency.”
“He mentioned the World Cup 2026 and Olympics 2028. That part is real-world relevant.”
“Saying Washington has ‘almost no crime anymore’ is… bold.”
“A trillion-dollar defense budget brag: some will cheer, some will panic.”
“Tax on tips and overtime is going to split even Democrats.”
“He says tariffs are paid by foreign countries. That’s disputed—consumers often pay more.”
“This speech has a lot of ‘they’re evil’ and not much ‘here’s the bill text.’”
“I’m pro-border security, but ‘zero illegal admitted in nine months’ sounds impossible.”
“He name-drops Charlie Kirk being murdered—if true, that’s massive news. I haven’t heard it.”
“He said 32,000 protesters killed by Iran ‘over the last couple months’—that’s an extraordinary claim.”
“The Medal of Honor segments are meant to humanize. It worked emotionally.”
“If recruitment is ‘stacked’ now, good. But show numbers.”
“He’s mixing policy, comedy, and grievance like it’s a rally. That’s his style.”
“He says GDP dropped 2 points due to a shutdown. That’s a big economic claim.”
“The Houston mom losing 20 bids to investment firms is real-life pain for buyers.”
“Banning ‘social transitions’ at school is complicated—schools, parents, and kids’ privacy collide.”
“I’m not mad about ‘protecting home values.’ People’s wealth is tied up there.”
“But you can’t lower rates and keep prices high and make housing affordable. Pick two.”
“He’s saying Congress doesn’t need to act on tariffs—executive power expansion vibes.”
“The speech is packed with claims that should be fact-checked line-by-line.”
“From Canada: the ‘hottest country in the world’ line feels like chest-thumping. We care more about whether U.S. trade policy whiplashes our exports.”
“The tariff talk matters for Canada—when the U.S. swings tariffs, we feel it immediately.”
“Claiming allies are now paying 5% GDP for defense would be huge—hard to believe without confirmation.”
“The hockey segment will get Canadians’ attention… but not in the way he thinks.”
“From the UK: the NATO 5% claim is enormous if true. That would dominate British headlines.”
“The speech’s tone is very ‘campaign rally.’ That’s more American than British political culture.”
“Tariffs replacing income tax sounds like 19th-century economics dressed up as modern policy.”
“Lots of culture-war content woven into policy. That’s a deliberate strategy.”
“The ‘Somali pirates’ line is straight-up inflammatory.”
“As a Minnesotan, I’m asking: what program is he even talking about?”
“If fentanyl is down 56% like he claims, that would be incredible news.”
“The repeated ‘you should be ashamed’ stuff is pure confrontation.”
“The ‘TrumpRX’ website branding is… wild. Government programs shouldn’t be personal merch.”
“He says ‘we ended DEI in America.’ That’s not a simple switch you flip.”
“Legion of Merit award presentation mid-speech feels cinematic.”
“I noticed he kept praising ‘private sector’ jobs—he knows his audience.”
“The ‘ban transitioning children without parents’ line will be used in campaign ads tomorrow.”
“His 250-year history wrap-up was the strongest writing in the whole thing.”
“He’s claiming a Venezuela dictator was captured by U.S. forces—if that happened, it would be world-shaking.”
“Bottom line: either this is the greatest year in history or it’s the greatest speechwriter in history.”
